01-write-a-one-line-problem-statement.note: A private social network and intranet for one company's staff, white-labelled for resale.

01-list-your-users-and-roles.note: Staff plus Moderators, Communications, Organisation admins and Editors.

01-sketch-the-core-user-journey.note: Five tabs: Feed, Chat, News, Alerts, Menu.

01-talk-to-10-potential-users.note: Built from a review of the app Supreme uses today; the demo and pilot bring real users' views.

01-check-the-market.note: Compared feature by feature with the current TeamSupreme (Speakap) app.

01-run-a-smoke-test.note: Built for one client, Supreme; the demo replaces a waitlist.

01-list-the-data-the-idea-needs.note: The data is clear from the features; the written list belongs in the DPIA.

01-check-for-regulated-territory.note: UK GDPR applies to staff data; DPIA and privacy notice are on the go-live list.

01-decide-what-you-will-not-collect.note: Birthdays are opt-in, day and month only; usage figures are totals, never per person.

01-choose-web-mobile-or-both.note: Web app that can go on the home screen; native apps only if the pilot asks.

01-cut-to-one-core-workflow.note: It replaces an existing app, so it matches that app's features instead.

01-set-success-metrics.note: No targets for the pilot yet (for example weekly active staff).

01-budget-for-security-not-just-build.note: An independent security test is planned before full rollout.

02-write-user-stories-with-abuse-cases.note: Abuse limits, reports and evidence keeping show abuse was considered; not written as stories.

02-pick-a-security-baseline.note: No baseline such as OWASP ASVS chosen yet.

02-set-uptime-and-recovery-targets.note: No downtime or data-loss targets agreed with Supreme yet.

02-know-who-your-attackers-are.note: Insiders, leavers and floods are handled; not written up as a threat model.

02-adopt-a-secure-development-framework.note: Eight security rules every app follows.

02-make-security-part-of-done.note: Rules plus 145 tests; no checklist per change.

02-choose-a-home-for-tasks-and-docs.note: README and the feature plan; no task tracker.

02-record-architecture-decisions.note: Choices and known shortcuts are written in the README.

03-decide-build-hire-or-no-code.note: Built by Hivemark AI for Supreme.

03-get-ip-and-confidentiality-in-writing.note: No contract with Supreme found in the project.

03-turn-on-strong-mfa-everywhere.note: Supreme is to require MFA for the app in Entra Conditional Access.

03-create-a-break-glass-account.note: The first admin is the break-glass account; its password works only while password login is on.

03-register-your-domain-securely.note: Supreme provides the address (for example hub.supreme.co.uk).

03-set-up-spf-dkim-and-dmarc.note: Email goes through Supreme's own relay and domain.

03-set-up-your-code-host.note: The project has no git history: one bad edit or a lost laptop loses work.

03-keep-an-inventory-of-every-service.note: README lists every outside service: Entra, SMTP, push services, translation, the Fly demo.

04-prefer-managed-boring-tech.note: Django 5.2 LTS, Postgres and plain JavaScript; no front-end build.

04-follow-the-twelve-factor-app.note: Every setting comes from environment variables.

04-keep-the-attack-surface-small.note: Nine dependencies and no separate admin app.

04-frontend-framework.note: Server-rendered Django templates escape output by default.

04-database-type.note: Postgres 17 in production, SQLite for local work.

04-separate-dev-staging-and-production.note: Local, a demo with made-up data, and Supreme's servers; a test copy for Entra is still to set up.

04-keep-the-database-on-a-private-networ.note: Only nginx publishes a port; the database isn't reachable from outside.

04-split-admin-from-the-public-app.note: Admin is /admin/ in the same app; Supreme is to limit it to the office or VPN.

04-isolate-each-customer-s-data.note: Each company gets its own copy and database.

04-plan-for-failure.note: Services restart by themselves; one server, no standby.

04-map-every-third-party.note: Every outbound connection is listed for Supreme's IT.

05-build-a-data-inventory.note: The data export covers every section; the written inventory goes in the DPIA.

05-collect-the-minimum.note: Only names, emails and account status come from Entra; birthdays are opt-in.

05-pseudonymise-analytics-and-logs.note: Insights are totals only, with no individual tracking.

05-choose-the-data-region-on-purpose.note: Live data stays on Supreme's servers; the demo runs in London.

05-use-a-managed-database.note: Supreme's own servers by design; Postgres patching and backups are theirs.

05-put-files-in-object-storage.note: Files stay on Supreme's server and are served only after a permission check.

05-block-public-bucket-access.note: Upload folders are internal to nginx; the app checks every download first.

05-encrypt-in-transit-everywhere.note: HTTPS through Supreme's proxy; the HTTPS redirect and HSTS go on at go-live.

05-encrypt-at-rest-with-managed-keys.note: Encrypted disks are Supreme's to provide.

05-hash-passwords-properly.note: Staff sign in with SSO; Django hashes the break-glass password.

05-plan-key-rotation.note: No rotation plan yet for the secret key, the Entra secret or the push keys.

05-use-least-privilege-database-roles.note: The app connects as the database owner.

05-turn-on-row-level-security.note: One company per database; the app checks access on every request.

05-return-only-the-fields-needed.note: Pages are built on the server; no JSON API hands out whole records.

05-set-retention-periods.note: The daily clean-up is built; Supreme still has to choose the periods.

05-let-users-export-and-delete.note: Everyone can download their data as a zip; leavers' accounts go after the retention period.

05-back-up-with-the-3-2-1-rule.note: Backup commands are written; scheduling and off-site copies are Supreme's.

05-use-fake-data-outside-production.note: seed_demo makes up colleagues; the demo server holds no real staff data.

06-use-a-proven-login-provider.note: Single sign-on with Entra ID or Google through mozilla-django-oidc, with PKCE.

06-offer-passkeys-and-mfa.note: MFA comes from Entra; Supreme turns it on with Conditional Access.

06-follow-modern-password-rules.note: Staff have no passwords here; they sign in with their work account.

06-don-t-reveal-which-emails-exist.note: No sign-up or password sign-in in production.

06-keep-sessions-in-secure-cookies.note: Session and CSRF cookies are secure outside development.

06-validate-tokens-strictly.note: RS256, the tenant's keys, PKCE, and the shared Microsoft endpoints refused.

06-check-permission-on-every-request.note: Every page needs sign-in and every action is checked on the server; 79 test checks cover refusals.

06-model-roles-and-permissions.note: Moderators, Communications, Organisation admins and Editors, with fine-grained permissions.

06-use-unguessable-ids-in-urls.note: Numbered IDs; the permission checks protect them.

06-grant-least-privilege.note: Each role gets only the permissions it needs.

06-use-single-sign-on-for-internal-tools.note: Admins sign in with their work account too.

06-build-an-audited-admin-panel.note: The admin is the moderation desk; moderator actions and deletions go to a read-only audit log.

06-offboard-within-hours.note: Leavers are signed out within 15 minutes and switched off nightly.

06-no-long-lived-cloud-keys.note: The Entra app uses a client secret; the README recommends a certificate.

07-learn-the-owasp-top-10.note: The rules cover access checks, escaping, CSRF, uploads and outbound requests.

07-validate-every-input-on-the-server.note: Django forms on every write; uploads checked by their content.

07-escape-output-avoid-raw-html.note: Text is escaped before any formatting; links must start with http(s).

07-handle-file-uploads-safely.note: Checked by content, photos re-encoded, videos stripped of metadata, served after a permission check.

07-block-server-side-request-forgery.note: Push only goes to the known push services; translation only to the configured server.

07-fail-safely.note: Debug is off unless set, and the app won't start without a secret key.

07-keep-secrets-out-of-code.note: Secrets come from the environment; .env is ignored and kept out of the Docker image.

07-know-which-keys-may-be-public.note: Only the push public key reaches the browser.

07-automate-dependency-updates.note: Versions are pinned but nothing checks for updates.

07-scan-for-known-vulnerabilities.note: pip-audit is suggested in the README but not run on a schedule.

07-vet-new-packages-before-adding.note: No new dependency without a strong reason.

07-commit-lockfiles-pin-versions.note: Exact versions pinned; no hashes and no git yet.

07-review-ai-generated-code.note: Built with an AI assistant; 145 tests check behaviour, but no second reviewer.

07-defend-against-prompt-injection.note: No AI features; an assistant waits for a data-protection decision.

07-limit-data-sent-to-ai-providers.note: Translation is self-hosted; monitoring bots need Supreme's approval as sub-processors.

08-write-user-a-vs-user-b-tests.note: 79 test checks that people are refused what they mustn't see or change.

08-get-a-penetration-test-before-launch.note: Planned before full rollout; not booked yet.

09-know-the-shared-responsibility-model.note: The README splits what the code does from what Supreme must do.

09-check-certifications-and-a-dpa.note: No data processing agreement with Supreme found.

09-pin-every-data-region.note: Supreme's own servers for live data; London for the demo.

09-match-the-host-to-your-team.note: Docker Compose on Supreme's servers, with a written list for their IT.

09-fly-io.note: The public demo runs on Fly.io in London, with made-up data.

09-protect-preview-links.note: The demo is public but holds only made-up data; its sign-ins are reset per visitor.

09-harden-any-server-you-run.note: A firewall so only the proxy reaches the app, and monthly patching, are on Supreme's list.

09-app-store-accounts.note: Home-screen web app; no app stores.

09-put-a-cdn-and-firewall-in-front.note: Supreme's load balancer sits in front; nginx limits requests.

09-transactional-email-service.note: Daily digests and alerts go through Supreme's SMTP relay.

10-automate-build-test-and-deploy.note: Deploys are by hand (git pull and docker compose); no pipeline yet.

10-migrate-databases-safely.note: Migrations run on start; a backup before each update isn't automatic.

10-minimal-non-root-images.note: Slim Python image, running as the app user.

10-never-bake-secrets-into-images.note: Only a throwaway key is used at build; .env stays out of the image.

11-privacy-policy.note: House rules carry a data notice; the staff privacy notice is still to write.

11-terms-of-service.note: Everyone accepts the house rules on first sign-in; HR still has to approve the text.

11-gdpr-and-uk-gdpr-basics.note: Export, retention and minimisation are built; DPIA and notice to do.

11-assess-high-risk-processing.note: A DPIA is on the go-live list.

11-answer-data-requests-on-time.note: Staff can download their own data; Supreme's HR handles formal requests.

11-sign-a-dpa-with-every-processor.note: Data processing agreement between Hivemark AI and Supreme still to sign.

11-industry-specific-rules.note: No card, health or children's data.

11-eu-cyber-resilience-act.note: Sold in the UK; check again before selling into the EU.

12-set-security-headers.note: Content Security Policy, no framing, referrer and permissions rules.

12-configure-cors-tightly.note: No cross-site API, so browsers block other sites by default.

12-defend-against-csrf.note: Every write is a POST with Django's CSRF token.

12-rate-limit-everything-public.note: nginx limits pages and sign-in; the app limits posts, uploads, comments and reports per person.

12-turn-on-a-waf-and-ddos-protection.note: Up to Supreme's network in front of the server.

12-close-dev-paths-and-endpoints.note: Supreme is to limit /admin/ to the office or VPN.

12-check-search-engine-indexing.note: Every page needs sign-in, so nothing can be indexed.

12-delete-test-accounts-and-defaults.note: Demo sign-ins exist only on the demo server; production uses SSO.

12-run-the-launch-checklist.note: The README has a go-live list for Supreme's side.

12-have-the-incident-plan-ready.note: A breach plan is on the go-live list.

12-set-up-a-status-page.note: Internal app on Supreme's own servers.

12-launch-in-stages.note: A pilot with one department comes before full rollout.

13-log-security-events.note: Sign-ins, failures, deletions, moderation, limits, exports and deactivations go to a JSON security log.

13-never-log-secrets-or-personal-data.note: The security log names the person by design; not checked for tokens yet.

13-centralise-and-protect-logs.note: JSON lines are ready for Supreme's security monitoring; the connection is theirs.

13-uptime-checks-from-outside.note: No outside uptime check yet; it needs no access to content.

13-alert-on-suspicious-activity.note: Disk and directory-sync problems are emailed; security alerts depend on Supreme's monitoring.

13-make-sure-a-human-sees-alerts.note: ADMIN_EMAILS get disk and sync alerts.

14-write-an-incident-response-plan.note: A breach plan is on the go-live list (ICO within 72 hours).

14-build-kill-switches.note: Entra switches people off in 15 minutes and moderators hide content in one click; no switch to close the hub.

14-notify-within-the-legal-deadline.note: The 72-hour ICO deadline is noted; the plan isn't written.

15-patch-on-a-schedule.note: Monthly patching is on Supreme's list; nothing scheduled yet.

15-track-end-of-life-dates.note: Django 5.2 LTS gets security fixes until April 2028.

15-version-releases-clearly.note: Version 2, with What's new notes in the admin.

15-confirm-deletion-jobs-run.note: The daily purge exists; check it runs once retention is set.

single-tenant-sign-in.t: Only Supreme's own tenant can sign in
single-tenant-sign-in.s: Settings refuse the shared Microsoft endpoints, and only company email domains get in.

leavers-in-15-minutes.s: Sign-in is re-checked every 15 minutes, and a nightly Entra check switches leavers off.

entra-certificate.t: Entra app uses a certificate, not a secret
entra-certificate.s: A certificate can't be copied as easily as a client secret.
entra-certificate.note: Recommended in the README before go-live.

evidence-kept-30-days.t: Deleted posts kept 30 days for HR
evidence-kept-30-days.s: Nobody can destroy evidence before HR sees a report.

uploads-lose-location.t: Photos and videos lose location data
uploads-lose-location.s: Photos are re-encoded and videos copied without metadata.

demo-sign-ins-file.t: Keep demo sign-ins out of the code folder
demo-sign-ins-file.s: demo-logins.txt sits next to the code; keep it out of any repository and share sign-ins another way.
demo-sign-ins-file.note: Already kept out of the Docker image.

admin-office-only.t: Admin pages only from the office or VPN

it-checklist-sent.t: Supreme's IT has the server checklist
it-checklist-sent.s: Server, HTTPS address, Entra app, SMTP relay, proxy address, outbound push, optional translation.
it-checklist-sent.note: Written in the README; not yet confirmed with Supreme's IT.

house-rules-approved.t: House rules approved by Supreme HR
house-rules-approved.s: The text is a starting point, not legal advice; HR and data protection sign it off.

bots-need-approval.t: No bot reads staff content without Supreme's OK
bots-need-approval.s: Any bot that reads logs sends staff data to its AI provider, so it needs approval as a sub-processor first.

p01.title: Put the code under version control
p01.why: There's no git history: one bad edit or a lost laptop loses the work.

p02.title: Demo ready: Supreme branding and sample data
p02.why: The demo is the first step in the plan.

p04.title: Dependency checks and code scanning
p04.why: Catches known holes before Supreme's security test does.

p05.title: Test server, HTTPS and Entra test app
p05.why: Supreme's IT does this; we answer their questions.

p07.title: Paperwork: DPIA, privacy notice, retention, house rules
p07.why: Needed before real staff data goes in.

p08.title: Book the independent security test
p08.why: Testers book up: book in December for early February.

p09.title: Backups, restore test and uptime alerts
p09.why: Prove recovery works before the pilot grows.

p11.title: Pilot with one department
p11.why: A few weeks of real use before everyone joins.

p12.title: Incident plan, named moderators, HR route
p12.why: Who does what when something goes wrong.

p13.title: Fix what the pilot finds
p13.why: Small releases while the pilot runs.

p14.title: Security test, then fix its findings

p15.title: Go / no-go for full rollout
p15.why: Only with the security test's findings fixed.

p16.title: Full rollout to all staff
p16.why: About 500 people, in waves by department.

p17.title: All staff on One Supreme
p17.why: The goal by the end of February.

20261118-1610-first-review.text: First review from the code: 69 done, 48 in progress, 46 not needed. Roadmap drafted to 28 Feb. ONE SUPREME to confirm.

project.name: One Supreme
project.about: Supreme PLC's staff hub: a private social network and intranet for about 500 staff. Version 2 is built; the demo, a pilot and full rollout come next.
project.roadmap_note: Draft dates from the README's plan. ONE SUPREME and Vince adjust them as the work moves.
